subject.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans

question: Should OpenClaw treat valid under-4-MiB ignore files with more than 20,000 patterns or a pattern over 16 KiB as unreadable and hide their entire workspace subtree?
rationale: The byte cap addresses memory allocation, while the added rule-count and rule-length limits introduce a separate user-visible compatibility contract that cannot be selected mechanically.

options.title: Preserve valid ignore semantics
options.body: Remove the pattern-count and pattern-length fail-closed limits, retaining only the bounded file read and failure handling for genuinely oversized or unreadable files.

options.title: Adopt complexity limits explicitly
options.body: Keep the limits only with clear maintainer approval, documented behavior, and focused proof showing the intended upgrade impact on real workspaces.

recommendation.title: Preserve valid ignore semantics
recommendation.body: Remove the pattern-count and pattern-length fail-closed limits, retaining only the bounded file read and failure handling for genuinely oversized or unreadable files.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-head scan-policy commits and assignment connect steipete most directly to the compatibility decision.
